kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA margin as a percentage of revenue, a key measure of operating profitability.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 14.2% in 2025, up 40 basis points from 13.8% in 2024, reflecting a structural improvement of 370 basis points since 2022 (10.7%). This improvement results from pricing discipline, an SG&A efficiency program delivering EUR 200 million in gross cost reductions, and a manufacturing excellence program including six site closures.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue in millions of euros for fiscal year 2025.
kpis.description: Revenue totaled EUR 10.158 billion in 2025, down 5.2% from EUR 10.711 billion in 2024, reflecting soft market conditions and geopolitical challenges. The decline was mitigated by maintained pricing discipline and effective cost management.
kpis.signal: Market pressure contained through operational efficiency

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA in millions of euros, measuring operating cash flow generation capacity.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA totaled EUR 1.444 billion in 2025, down 2.3% from EUR 1.478 billion in 2024, but up 24.8% since 2022 (EUR 1.157 billion), demonstrating the impact of structural margin improvement on value creation despite market headwinds.
kpis.signal: Stability in operating value creation despite revenue decline

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Operating income in millions of euros for fiscal year 2025.
kpis.description: Operating income reached EUR 1.164 billion in 2025, reflecting solid operating performance driven by execution of SG&A efficiency and manufacturing excellence programs, despite geopolitical challenges, tariffs, and foreign exchange impacts.
kpis.signal: Robust operating profitability in a challenging market environment

kpis.name: Total Employees (FTE)
kpis.explanation: Total number of full-time equivalents employed by AkzoNobel in 2025.
kpis.description: AkzoNobel employs 31,500 full-time equivalents in 2025, operating in more than 150 countries to support a world-class brand portfolio including Dulux, International, Sikkens, and Interpon.
kpis.signal: Global talent team spanning more than 150 countries

kpis.name: Carbon Footprint Reduction (Scopes 1 and 2)
kpis.explanation: Percentage reduction in carbon footprint (scopes 1 and 2) compared to the 2018 baseline.
kpis.description: AkzoNobel reduced its carbon footprint (scopes 1 and 2) by 47% compared to the 2018 baseline, versus 41% in 2024, demonstrating sustained progress in decarbonization. This progress reflects investments in renewable energy, including a EUR 50 million upgrade at the Waukegan aerospace facility and adoption of wind and solar energy.
kpis.signal: Sustainability leadership with consistent annual progress toward climate targets

kpis.name: Return on Investment
kpis.explanation: Return on investment measured as a percentage for the year 2025.
kpis.description: Return on investment reached 13.5% in 2025, reflecting structural operational improvement and dynamic portfolio management, including the completion of the Akzo Nobel India Limited divestiture at 25x EBITDA and continued optimization of positioning in decorative paints in Southeast Asia.
kpis.signal: Capital efficiency reflecting operational improvement and portfolio management

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Earnings per share in euros for fiscal year 2025.
kpis.description: Earnings per share totaled EUR 3.71 in 2025, reflecting solid operating performance and improved profitability despite a challenging market environment.
kpis.signal: Shareholder value creation supported by profitability improvement

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of EUR 1.54 in the most recent year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders through annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of EUR 0.382 billion in the most recent year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Percentage of net income distributed as dividends: 60.2% in the most recent year.

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by weighted average diluted shares outstanding for the fiscal year. Illustrates the company's ability to generate earnings per share: the basis for calculating the Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Goodwill and Brand Impairment Risk for Decorative Paints China and North Asia
risks.summary: The Decorative Paints China & North Asia unit exhibits historically unfavorable revenue trends and is undergoing a major centralized reorganization in 2025, creating a high risk of impairment for EUR 408 million of goodwill and indefinite-lived brand assets (including the Dulux brand). A complex impairment test with sensitive assumptions (sales growth, margins, discount rates) is required annually.
risks.score_rationale: Identified as a new Key Audit Matter in 2025, with EUR 408 million of assets at risk; intense language ('historical revenue trends', 'significant management judgment', major organizational transition); deteriorating trend in DP CNA historical revenues; high balance sheet impact category.

risks.title: Major Litigation Project Ichthys: Potentially Insufficient EUR 300 Million Provision
risks.summary: AkzoNobel recorded a EUR 300 million provision in 2025 for Project Ichthys (legal proceedings involving current and former subsidiaries), but other elements of the litigation remain as unprovisioned contingent liabilities. An unfavorable outcome in these proceedings could generate significant additional charges, with legal complexity requiring external specialized expertise.
risks.score_rationale: New Key Audit Matter in 2025 with EUR 300 million provision recorded in Q3 2025 and additional unprovisioned contingent liabilities; very strong language ('can be significant for the Group's financial statements as a whole', 'specialized legal expertise'); sharply increased risk; potential financial exposure exceeding the provisioned amount.

risks.title: Risk of Fraud and Override of Internal Controls by Management
risks.summary: Auditors identified a fraud risk related to management's ability to override internal controls, particularly through unauthorized journal entries and biased estimates. This risk is inherent to AkzoNobel's decentralized structure operating across numerous jurisdictions, with complex consolidation processes.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned as a priority audit risk in the statutory auditors' report; moderate but structural language ('management is in a unique position to perpetrate fraud'); stable and recurring risk in large multinationals; potential impact on the group's financial credibility.

risks.title: Risk of Fraudulent Revenue Recognition Related to Growth Strategy
risks.summary: AkzoNobel's aggressive growth and market share expansion strategy creates pressure on revenue recognition, with an identified risk of recording unrealized or anticipated transactions. Auditors performed data analytics on journal entries related to revenues and year-end receivables balances.
risks.score_rationale: Identified as a specific fraud risk linked to AkzoNobel's growth and market share expansion strategy; direct language ('strategy to continuously grow and expand market share'); stable risk; impact on the reliability of published financial statements.

risks.title: Defined Benefit Pension Obligations: EUR 7.7 Billion UK Exposure
risks.summary: AkzoNobel carries EUR 7.7 billion in defined benefit pension obligations, primarily in the United Kingdom (ICI Pension Fund and Akzo Nobel CPS Scheme), partially covered by EUR 8.3 billion in plan assets. Any variation in key actuarial assumptions (discount rate, inflation, life expectancy) can generate significant actuarial variances impacting the group's equity and cash position.
risks.score_rationale: Recurring Key Audit Matter with DBO of EUR 7.7 billion (ICI Pension Fund and Akzo Nobel CPS Scheme representing 89% of total); high sensitivity to actuarial assumptions (discount rate, inflation, longevity); stable trend but massive structural exposure; high balance sheet impact category.

risks.title: Recoverability of Deferred Tax Assets in the Netherlands and United Kingdom
risks.summary: AkzoNobel holds significant deferred tax assets in the Netherlands and United Kingdom (EUR 403 million combined), whose recoverability depends on the realization of future taxable profits and execution of tax planning strategies. Local tax regulatory changes (interest limitation rules, rate modifications) could challenge these assets.
risks.score_rationale: Key Audit Matter with EUR 224 million in tax credits and EUR 179 million in tax loss carryforwards; high complexity related to local tax rules (interest limitation, specific credits); stable trend; dependence on future profit projections and tax planning strategies.

risks.title: Decorative Paints Structural Reorganization: Execution and Transition Risks
risks.summary: AkzoNobel initiated a major reorganization of its Decorative Paints division in 2025 toward a more globally centralized model, notably modifying the treatment of the Dulux brand in valuation models. This transition creates operational execution risks, potential loss of local talent, and cost structure misalignment, particularly critical in struggling Asian markets.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in the DP CNA impairment test context as an aggravating factor in 2025 ('transition to a new, more centralized organizational structure for the global Decorative Paints business'); newly identified risk; direct impact on asset valuation and operating performance; increasing trend.

risks.title: Multiple Legal Proceedings with Governments and Environmental Authorities
risks.summary: AkzoNobel and certain of its subsidiaries (current and former) face multiple legal proceedings involving governments, tax authorities, and environmental agencies in several countries. Environmental exposure is particularly significant for a paints and coatings manufacturer using regulated chemical substances, with increasing remediation and penalty risks.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in the Project Ichthys context ('legal proceedings, as well as proceedings by/discussions with, governments, tax authorities, environmental agencies'); moderate language but multi-jurisdictional exposure; stable to increasing trend given strengthening global environmental regulations; potential impact on reputation and finances.
